Nel sospetto ictus la prima domanda alla: In suspected stroke, the first question on non-contrast CT is: is there blood? Acute blood is hyperdense (about 50-80 HU) compared with brain parenchyma (30-40 HU) and is best seen with a narrow window (centre 35-40, width 40-80). If there is haemorrhage, thrombolysis is contraindicated and the whole pathway changes: rapid blood pressure control, reversal of any anticoagulants, neurosurgical assessment. The report must give the site, volume (A×B×C/2 formula: the three largest diameters in cm multiplied and divided by two), ventricular extension, mass effect and midline shift, hydrocephalus. Putamen, thalamus, pons and cerebellum are the typical sites of hypertensive haemorrhage; a lobar site in a young patient or an atypical appearance prompts a search for other causes (vascular malformations, venous thrombosis, tumour) with CT angiography or MRI. Even in a deep location, under 45 years of age as in this patient, the AHA/ASA 2022 guidelines advise completing with CT angiography. Here the haematoma is small, with no intraventricular blood or shift: relatively good prognosis, but it must be reported immediately.
